purpose: An OME-Zarr (OME-NGFF) reader/writer extension for 3D Slicer that loads local, https:// and s3:// multiscale image stores at a chosen resolution, refines slice views, and writes volumes/labels back as OME-Zarr. It is for microscopy and medical-volume users who work with chunked multiscale stores.
summary: I inspected the catalog entry, CMakeLists, README/TUTORIAL, the CI workflow, the test runner, and the relevant parts of OMEZarr/OMEZarr.py (helpers, ensureNgffZarr, storageOptions, writeVolume, the settings panel, and test teardown). The module installs ngff-zarr>=0.52.0 via pip only after a confirmation dialog in interactive use, and it does not install torch or pin Slicer-bundled packages. S3 is read anonymously unless credentials are supplied. I found no malicious or concealed behaviour and no blocking issue. The catalog entry is minimal but mechanically sound. Remaining gaps are listed below.

safety.rationale: Inspected ensureNgffZarr (OMEZarr.py:382-397), storageOptions (399-422), readStoreAttributes (157-186), writeVolume (1720-1760) and the test tearDown (2621-2625). The network fetch is only for a user-supplied URL, S3 defaults to anonymous, and rmtree targets a fresh slicer.util.tempDirectory. No pickle, eval, exec or subprocess was found in the module.

environment.rationale: The module calls slicer.util.pip_install('ngff-zarr[remote]>=0.52.0') at OMEZarr.py:394, gated by a confirmation dialog when interactive. ngff-zarr[remote] may pull transitive dependencies (for example obstore, dask, zarr) into Slicer's Python, which I could not resolve. There is no torch or Qt/VTK-bundling package.

packaging.rationale: CMakeLists.txt sets EXTENSION_DEPENDS to NA, which matches build_dependencies []. OMEZarr/CMakeLists.txt installs OMEZarr.py and the icon via slicerMacroBuildScriptedModule. The CI workflow builds and runs the self-test on Linux, macOS and Windows.

license.rationale: LICENSE is MIT (Copyright 2026 Fideus Labs LLC). README.md:140 states MIT. ngff-zarr is installed from PyPI at runtime and is not bundled.

soundness.rationale: The module uses dask/lazy reads with progress and cancel (README). Module-level code is light. The settings-panel lambda at OMEZarr.py:2312 passes self.storageOptionsEdit.text, which is an attribute, not a call result, so it appears to be correct in PyQt-style access, but I did not verify this against the Slicer Python API. The module relies on a pip install at runtime, and the test suite is large (about 3500 lines).

utility.rationale: README.md and TUTORIAL.md document usage, the Python API and limitations, with screenshots and a video. A headless self-test runs in CI on three platforms. Tier 1 is appropriate for a new extension. The README's 'Still to do' section openly lists known limitations.

findings.title: Runtime pip install of ngff-zarr pulls transitive dependencies into Slicer's Python
findings.explanation: OMEZarr.py:386-394 installs 'ngff-zarr[remote]>=0.52.0' into Slicer's shared Python when a store is opened. The install is confirmed interactively but not in testing mode. Transitive dependencies could downgrade or conflict with packages Slicer bundles (for example numpy or requests). I did not verify the resolved dependency set, so the risk is unverified.
findings.suggestion: Document the resolved dependency set. Confirm the install does not downgrade Slicer-bundled packages, and state the install in the extension description.

findings.title: Could not confirm the settings-panel editingFinished lambda
findings.explanation: OMEZarr.py:2312 passes self.storageOptionsEdit.text as a value to Settings.set. I did not check whether the Qt binding exposes this as a property or a method, so the stored value may be wrong. This is a minor, unverified bug candidate, not a safety issue.
findings.suggestion: Confirm the attribute access works in Slicer's Qt bindings, or use .text() and test that the setting persists.
